supported: Independent mapped Torgersen breeding footprints show strong contraction from 23 historic sub-colonies to five active footprints by 2022.
Spatial attrition is non-random with respect to physical habitat: all historic south-aspect sub-colonies are extinct while five north-aspect footprints remain active.
Larger historic sub-colonies tended to persist longer, providing an external spatial correlate of local persistence.
These mapped patterns converge at the phenomenon level with the census-derived result that a more distributed breeder configuration carries modest positive next-year demographic information.
not_supported: one-to-one validation of Palmer LTER colony_code against the independent GIS polygon identifiers
a causal claim that physical habitat fragmentation causes the effective-colony-number predictive signal
equivalence between effective colony number and mapped habitat area or connectivity
a claim that larger breeding groups are intrinsically protective

crosswalk_status.consequence: Use spatial evidence as independent process-level triangulation only; retain the causal and identifier-level validation boundary.

manuscript_role: Strengthens Discussion D4 from an unvalidated topology interpretation to external phenomenon-level spatial convergence while preserving the unresolved colony-ID crosswalk caveat.
next_gate: Core ecological result family is closed. Proceed to figure-data exports, reproducibility checks and manuscript packaging unless an external colony-code/polygon crosswalk becomes available.
